summary: Client-side prefetch queue + reconnects causing missed idempotency header and duplicated funcall acks across SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on BeaconHealth's dedicated deployment report duplicated external tool/webhook invocations and missing ack visibility when clients use the SDK prefetch/buffered-sender feature combined with long-running streaming sessions.

Impact:
- Duplicate side-effects observed in customer systems (double POSTs to downstream tools) for ~0.8% of streaming sessions that were active >30s.
- Billing noise due to re-executed tool work.
- Customer has temporarily disabled prefetch, impacting throughput and latency.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-west (customer-owned capacity).
- SDKs in use: go (v1.11.0), python (v2.0.4), ts (v0.9.7); all using client-side prefetch/buffering with background token refresh enabled.
- Model: redwood/gptx-8k-v1 pinned in routing policy.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session with a chain of function/tool calls (external webhook that creates an order).
2) Enable client prefetch/buffer of 10 messages and enable background token refresh.
3) Simulate a short network hiccup or proxy 503 (edge) causing reconnect and resume.
4) Observe duplicate POSTs to downstream webhook within seconds of the resume.

Observed behavior:
- On reconnect, some SDKs re-sent buffered messages but the idempotency header (X-Idempotency-Key) was either missing or truncated on one of the resend attempts, resulting in the server accepting the call as a new invocation.
- Acknowledgement tokens from our runtime (funcall ack) were sometimes applied to the resumed session but did not de-duplicate the downstream side-effect because the idempotency key didn't match.

Expected behavior:
- SDK should preserve per-action idempotency metadata across reconnects and replays, or the server should suppress duplicate downstream executions when the request body/hash matches within a short dedupe window.

Relevant logs/traces (samples):
- trace_id: 9f7a2e03-usw-2026-03-09-02:15:37 (shows reconnect and two POST attempts to customer webhook: 200 then 201).
- gateway logs: edge-proxy returned 503 at 02:15:36, client resumed at 02:15:38.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Alex Kim (Support): Customer opened reporting duplicate downstream webhook posts after SDK reconnects during streaming sessions. Provided trace_id and reproduction steps. Marked P1 due to side-effect duplication.
2026-03-10 - Priya Nair (Support Engineer): Acknowledged ticket. Asked customer for SDK versions and whether prefetch/buffering was enabled. Requested sample request/headers for the duplicated POSTs.

2026-03-11 - BeaconHealth (Customer): Attached sanitized headers for the two POSTs. Noted X-Idempotency-Key present on first POST but missing on second. Shared SDK config: prefetch=10, background_refresh=true.

2026-03-11 - Marcus Li (SDK Eng): Reproduced locally with go sdk v1.11.0 + artificial TCP reset. Observed buffered message replay where our local packet-split logic truncated the idempotency header when sending a chunked retry. Filed a PR to preserve headers across chunk splits. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ssr-sdk/pull/6789

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (Support Engineer): Rolled recommended mitigation to customer: upgrade SDK to patched client build (go v1.11.1-alpha), disable prefetch buffer (prefetch=0) until patch is applied, and add server-side webhook dedupe using X-Idempotency-Key. Customer applied workaround; duplicates dropped to 0.05%.
2026-03-12 - BeaconHealth (Customer): Confirms workaround effective; requested guidance for permanent fix and whether runtime dedupe window will be tuned for dedicated clusters.
investigation_notes:
Findings:
- Root cause appears to be interaction between client prefetch buffering and our chunked request/resume path. When buffered frames are re-emitted after a reconnect, a header boundary can be lost if the client re-chunks messages differently, resulting in either missing or truncated X-Idempotency-Key.
- Affected paths: streaming resume with buffered frames + background token refresh that triggers a simultaneous connection reset and resume.
- Reproducible across go and python SDKs (TS less frequent due to different internal buffering).

Hypotheses tested:
- Proxy edge 503 triggers immediate reconnect -> yes.
- SDK re-chunking behavior leads to header boundary loss -> confirmed in go repro.
- Server dedupe on body-hash would have prevented side-effect duplication in many cases, but we currently rely primarily on X-Idempotency-Key for tool dedupe.

Action items created:
1) SDK engineering: backport header-preservation fix to go/python/ts clients (PR linked). Priority: high.
2) Runtime: evaluate short dedupe-by-body/hash window (120s) for function/webhook invocations to catch cases when idempotency header is absent due to client-side truncation.
3) Support: surface clear guidance in SDK docs about prefetch implications and recommend per-action idempotency keys.
resolution:
Workaround and fix rollout:
- Short-term: Customer disabled prefetch buffer; implemented webhook-side dedup using X-Idempotency-Key and body-hash fallback. Support validated reduction in duplicates.
- Medium-term: SDK patch landed in go and python (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ssr-sdk/pull/6789). We released go v1.11.1 and python v2.0.5 candidate to BeaconHealth's dedicated cluster for validation on 2026-03-12.
- Long-term: Runtime team will prototype a 2-minute body-hash dedupe for tool/webhook invocations in dedicated environments; design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Runtime+tool+dedupe.

Follow-ups:
- SRE/Runtime to run gradual rollout of body-hash dedupe to dedicated clusters and monitor false-positive suppression rates (owner: Lara Gomez). Target ETA: 2026-04-02.
- SDK team to publish release notes and upgrade guide; add explicit docs about prefetch and token refresh interactions (owner: Marcus Li). Target ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Support to update KB article and notify customers with streaming+prefetch use patterns.

Status: In Progress (customer validated workaround; patches deployed to staging and a dedicated canary cluster; production rollout pending runtime dedupe decision).
